summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic pancreatitis, recurrent leg cellulitis, and asthma was readmitted with persistent malaise, shortness of breath, cough, and tachycardia following a recent pneumonia. She was found to have Strep viridans bacteremia, likely originating from a dental abscess in her right lower second bicuspid, which was confirmed on imaging and treated with tooth extraction. She was started on vancomycin, then transitioned to ceftriaxone after sensitivities confirmed susceptibility. Serial blood cultures cleared, and echocardiograms (TTE and TEE) showed no evidence of endocarditis. A PICC line was placed for outpatient IV antibiotic therapy. She also experienced transient atrial fibrillation attributed to infection, and nocturnal bradycardia with oxygen desaturation, prompting discharge on home oxygen at night and referral for a sleep study. Her reactive airway symptoms were managed with inhalers and benzonatate, and her diarrhea was deemed medication-related. She was discharged home with a plan for 14 days of IV ceftriaxone, follow-up with infectious disease, and outpatient evaluation for thyroid abnormality noted on imaging.
